# Zenvi tools

<!-- Generated by packages/engine/scripts/gen-tools-doc.ts from @zenvi/engine/tools. Do not edit by hand. -->

One tool catalog for every Zenvi surface: the Zenvi Assistant in the web editor, the local MCP server (`zenvi mcp`), the Zenvi Cloud remote MCP server, and the CLI. 110 tools: 95 of the 169 tools Zenvi desktop lists (zenvi-core develop `1f80cb3d061b`; same names, arguments and receipts) and 15 direct tools for coding agents. The other desktop tools are not ported yet (see [Not ported yet](#not-ported-yet)).

Every call returns a contract-3 receipt (`{contract: 3, status, tool, summary, clips, …, undoSteps}`); a failure's summary starts with `Error:`, and a surface limitation says `Error: <tool> is not available in this Zenvi surface: …` (do not retry). One call is at most one undo step.

## Where tools work

| Surface | Host | Works | Partial | Not available |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web editor (Zenvi Assistant, command palette) | `apps/editor/src/features/editor/assistant/host.ts` | 83 | 17 | 10 |
| CLI and local MCP server (zenvi, zenvi mcp) | `packages/render-node/src/host/node-host.ts` | 79 | 17 | 14 |
| Zenvi Cloud remote MCP server (ChatGPT, Claude.ai) | `packages/cloud/src/mcp/engine.ts` | 75 | 15 | 20 |
| Zenvi desktop | zenvi-core | 95 | 0 | 15 (direct tools are web-only) |

Availability follows each tool's required host capabilities and the host methods it calls at run time; the hosts are described in `SURFACE_PROFILES` (packages/engine/src/tools/availability.ts). Capabilities a session may lack (signed out of Zenvi, no WebCodecs export) are noted per tool.

- **Web editor (Zenvi Assistant, command palette)**: media, player, ui, exporter, frames, backend, storage, assets, audio; methods media.importUrl, media.pickFiles, media.writeGenerated, storage.readText, ui.openExportDialog, audio.decodePcm; only sometimes: exporter (browsers with WebCodecs export), backend (signed in to Zenvi).
- **CLI and local MCP server (zenvi, zenvi mcp)**: media, exporter, frames, audio, storage, backend, assets; methods media.importPath, media.listPaths, media.importUrl, media.writeGenerated, storage.open, storage.readText, storage.writeText, audio.decodePcm; only sometimes: backend (signed in with zenvi login).
- **Zenvi Cloud remote MCP server (ChatGPT, Claude.ai)**: media, frames, storage, assets, audio, backend; methods media.importUrl, media.writeGenerated, storage.readText, storage.writeText, audio.decodePcm; only sometimes: frames (the render worker is configured), media (ffprobe is available), assets (the engine's assets (title templates, emoji) are bundled), audio (ffmpeg is available), backend (the server is set up to call the Zenvi backend); hides 13 local-app tools.

## Tools

### get_project_info_tool

**Read project info**. Return project profile, fps, duration, and scale.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### list_files_tool

**List project media**. List media-bin files (paths, ids) — not timeline positions.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### list_clips_tool

**List clips**. List timeline clips with source_start/end, summary_preview, and occurrence_hint when duplicates exist.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layer` | string |  | Optional layer_number or UI track filter. |
| `detail_level` | string |  | summary (default) or full — accepted for Assistant/LLM compat; listing is always complete. |

### list_layers_tool

**List tracks**. List tracks/layers (ui_track and layer_number).

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### list_markers_tool

**List markers**. List every marker in the project.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### new_project_tool

**New project**. Create a new empty project.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor partial (only Zenvi desktop takes profile so far); cli partial (only Zenvi desktop takes profile so far); cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discard_unsaved` | boolean |  | Throw away unsaved changes in the current project. Only after the user agreed. (default false) |
| `profile` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Optional video profile or social preset for the new project, e.g. 'instagram_reel', 'youtube_4k', 'FHD 1080p 30 fps' (see list_project_profiles_tool). Empty = default profile. (default "") |
| `save_first` | boolean |  | Save the current project to its existing file first (it must have been saved before). (default false) |

### save_project_tool

**Save project**. Save the project to file_path (e.g.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: storage.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file_path` | string |  | Where to save. Empty = the project's current file (Save). A new path = Save As (.zvn is added when there is no project extension; missing folders are created). (default "") |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Allow replacing an existing file that is not this project's current file. (default false) |
| `path` | string |  | Where to save the project (.zvn is appended when missing). Omit to save to the current location. |

### open_project_tool

**Open project**. Open a project from file_path.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: storage.

Availability: editor — (needs opening project files); cli partial (only Zenvi desktop takes recent_index so far); cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discard_unsaved` | boolean |  | Throw away unsaved changes in the current project. Only after the user agreed. (default false) |
| `file_path` | string |  | Path of a .zvn project (legacy .osp/.flow also open). Leave empty when using recent_index. (default "") |
| `recent_index` | integer |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Open a recent project instead: 1 = most recent (see list_recent_projects_tool). 0 = use file_path. (default 0, min 0, max 10) |
| `save_first` | boolean |  | Save the current project to its existing file before opening the other one. (default false) |

### watch_clip_tool

**Load and play clip**. Play a clip in the editor preview: seek to a timeline clip (timeline_clip_id or query) and start playback.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: player.

Availability: editor partial (file_path needs local file access); cli — (needs playback); cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file_path` | string |  | Media path to import, place and play. |
| `query` | string |  | Describe the timeline clip to play. |
| `file_id` | string |  | Media-bin file to play (added to the timeline when it is not there yet). |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip to play. |

### watch_clip_window_tool

**Watch clip window**. Vision-check whether a query is actually visible in a window of a placed clip.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only, open world. Needs: frames, backend.

Availability: editor yes (only when signed in to Zenvi); cli yes (only when signed in with zenvi login); cloud yes (only when the render worker is configured and the server is set up to call the Zenvi backend); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string |  | What should be on screen in the window. |
| `start` | string \| number |  | Window start, source seconds (12, 12.5 or 0:12). Give start and end together, or neither to watch the best search match. |
| `end` | string \| number |  | Window end, source seconds. |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id (from list_clips_tool, get_timeline_state_tool or an earlier receipt). |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of passing an id: file name, subject, or words from its summary. Narrow it with track, occurrence or position_near. |
| `track` | string |  | Track: layer_number (preferred), track_id, the exact label, or ui_track counted from the bottom (1 = bottom). |
| `occurrence` | string \| number |  | 1-based pick when the query matches the same source several times (0 = best match). |
| `position_near` | string \| number \| null |  | Timeline seconds; only clips that span this time match. |

### play_tool

**Play / pause**. Control preview playback: action play, pause, toggle (default, like the Space bar), stop (pause and return to the start), or step_forward / step_back by frames.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only. Needs: player.

Availability: editor yes; cli — (needs playback); cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | "toggle" \| "play" \| "pause" \| "stop" \| "fast_forward" \| "rewind" \| "step_forward" \| "step_back" |  | What to do. play / pause (always pass one of these for a plain 'play' or 'pause'); toggle = the Space bar; stop = pause and return to the start; fast_forward / rewind = the L / J keys (one speed step faster forward / backward); step_forward / step_back = pause and move by `frames`. (default "toggle") |
| `frames` | integer |  | For step_forward / step_back: how many frames to move. (default 1, min 1, max 10000) |
| `speed` | integer \| null |  | For action='play': playback speed, 1 = normal, 2 or 4 = fast, -1 = backwards. Omit for normal speed. (min -16, max 16) |

### undo_tool

**Undo**. Undo the last action, or the last N actions.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | string \| number |  | Number of undo steps. (default 1) |

### redo_tool

**Redo**. Redo the last undone action, or the last N undone actions.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | string \| number |  | Number of redo steps (1-20). (default 1) |

### add_track_tool

**Add track**. Add empty tracks: on top (default, like the Add Track button), at the bottom, or above / below the track in relative_to.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer |  | How many tracks to add in this one step. With a name they are called '<name> 1' .. '<name> N' from bottom to top. (default 1, min 1, max 10) |
| `name` | string |  | Name shown in the new track's header, e.g. 'Music'. Empty = the default 'Track N'. (default "") |
| `position` | "top" \| "bottom" \| "above" \| "below" |  | Where the new track goes: 'top' (above every track, like the Add Track button), 'bottom' (below every track), or 'above' / 'below' the track in relative_to (Track menu > Add Track Above / Below). (default "top") |
| `relative_to` | string |  | For position 'above' / 'below': the existing track, as a UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, track id (L3) or layer number. (default "") |
| `label` | string |  | Alias for name. |

### add_marker_tool

**Add marker**. Add a timeline marker at position_seconds (default: the playhead), with a name and a colour tag.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | "blue" \| "red" \| "green" \| "yellow" \| "orange" \| "purple" \| "pink" \| "white" |  | Marker color tag; the timeline tints the marker's icon with it (blue = the default icon) and shows the marker's name next to it. (default "blue") |
| `name` | string |  | Marker name, e.g. 'Drop', 'Chorus', 'Cut here'. Used to find it again. (default "") |

### add_effect_tool

**Add effect**. Add a libopenshot effect (EffectInfo class_name such as Blur, Brightness, Saturation, ChromaKey) to one timeline clip, with its default parameters.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor partial (only Zenvi desktop takes processing, properties, scope, timeline_clip_ids so far); cli partial (only Zenvi desktop takes processing, properties, scope, timeline_clip_ids so far); cloud partial (only Zenvi desktop takes processing, properties, scope, timeline_clip_ids so far); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id. (default "") |
| `effect` | string |  | Effect to add: class or display name from list_effects_tool (Blur, Sharpen, ChromaKey, ColorGrade, Pixelate, Compressor, Echo, ParametricEQ...). (default "") |
| `effect_name` | string |  | Same as effect (either works). (default "") |
| `if_exists` | "update" \| "add" |  | When the clip already has this effect: 'update' changes that one (default, avoids stacking duplicates); 'add' stacks another copy. (default "update") |
| `interpolation` | "bezier" \| "linear" \| "constant" |  | Default interpolation for keyframes that do not name one. (default "bezier") |
| `occurrence` | integer |  | With clip_query: take the Nth match (1 = first). 0 = the best match. (default 0, min 0) |
| `position_near` | number \| null |  | With clip_query: prefer the clip nearest this timeline time (seconds). |
| `processing` | object |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Only for Stabilizer, Tracker, ObjectDetection, ObjectMask: the analysis options, same names as process_clip_effect_tool (smoothing, region, region_time, tracker_type, model, device, download_model, class_filter, confidence, points, negative_points, boxes, mask_quality). |
| `properties` | object |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Effect properties to set, as {name: value}. A value is a number, true/false, a choice name ("HSV/HSL hue"), a color ("#00ff00") or text; or keyframes [{"time": 2.0, "value": 10, "interpolation": "linear"}] in timeline seconds to animate it. list_effects_tool(effect=...) lists every property with its range, default and choices. |
| `scope` | "" \| "selected" \| "track" \| "all" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on `track`, 'all' = every clip. Clips that cannot take the effect (locked track, no picture/sound) are skipped and listed. (default "") |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred. (default "") |
| `timeline_clip_ids` | string[] |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Several timeline clip ids to change in one step. |
| `track` | string |  | Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number. (default "") |

### add_title_tool

**Add title**. Create a title / lower-third from a bundled SVG template with your text and place it on the timeline (default 5 s at 0 s).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media, assets.

Availability: editor partial (only Zenvi desktop takes background_color, fade_in_seconds, fade_out_seconds, font, font_scale, font_style, font_weight, lines, screen_position, subtitle, text_color so far); cli partial (only Zenvi desktop takes background_color, fade_in_seconds, fade_out_seconds, font, font_scale, font_style, font_weight, lines, screen_position, subtitle, text_color so far); cloud partial (only Zenvi desktop takes background_color, fade_in_seconds, fade_out_seconds, font, font_scale, font_style, font_weight, lines, screen_position, subtitle, text_color so far; only when ffprobe is available and the engine's assets (title templates, emoji) are bundled); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `background_color` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Colour of the title's full-frame background (transparent in most templates) with optional alpha, e.g. '#000000' for a solid black end card or '#00000080' for a 50% dark veil over the video. Empty keeps it. (default "") |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | How long the title stays on screen, in seconds. (default 5, min 0.01, max 86400) |
| `fade_in_seconds` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Fade the title in over this many seconds (0 = appear at once). (default 0, min 0, max 10) |
| `fade_out_seconds` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Fade the title out over this many seconds (0 = disappear at once). (default 0, min 0, max 10) |
| `file_name` | string |  | Name for the new title file in Project Files (without .svg). Empty = from the text. An existing name gets ' (1)', ' (2)'... instead of being overwritten. (default "") |
| `fit_text` | boolean |  | Shrink a line whose text would run off the frame (templates do not wrap text). (default true) |
| `font` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Font family for every line, e.g. 'Arial Black', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Georgia'. Must be installed; empty keeps the template's font. (default "") |
| `font_scale` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Text size relative to the template: 1 = as designed, 1.5 = half again as big, 0.7 = smaller. (default 1, min 0.2, max 5) |
| `font_style` | "" \| "italic" \| "normal" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Italic or upright text; empty keeps the template's. (default "") |
| `font_weight` | "" \| "bold" \| "normal" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Make the text bold or normal weight; empty keeps the template's. (default "") |
| `lines` | string[] |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Every field in order (as listed by list_title_templates_tool), for templates with several lines such as Standard_4 or credits. Overrides text/subtitle; fields left out are blanked. |
| `position_seconds` | number |  | Timeline second where the title starts. (default 0, min 0) |
| `screen_position` | "auto" \| "top" \| "center" \| "bottom" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Where the 16:9 title artboard sits when the project is not 16:9 (vertical reels, square): auto = by where the template's text is (lower thirds at the bottom, headers at the top). On 9:16 video bottom/top titles are lifted clear of the platform UI bands. (default "auto") |
| `subtitle` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Text for the template's subtitle field (second line), e.g. a role under a name. (default "") |
| `template` | string |  | Template name from list_title_templates_tool (e.g. 'Standard_1', 'Gray_Box_4', 'Bar_3', 'OpenShot'), or the path of an existing .svg title to start from. Empty = Bar_1 (centre title on a blue bar). (default "") |
| `text` | string |  | Main title text, e.g. 'Tokyo Day 1'. A '\n' puts the rest on the template's next field(s): 'Jane Doe\nFounder' fills a lower third's name and role. (default "") |
| `text_color` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Colour of every line: '#RRGGBB', '#RRGGBBAA' (alpha = opacity), 'rgba(r,g,b,a)' or a basic name ('white', 'yellow'). Empty keeps the template's colours. (default "") |
| `track` | string |  | UI track number (1 = bottom), name or layer for the title. Empty = the lowest free track above every clip with video at that time (a new top track when none is free). (default "") |

### add_captions_tool

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media, assets.

Availability: editor partial (captions come from indexed transcripts or an SRT/VTT file; the desktop also transcribes on device; only Zenvi desktop takes background_color, background_opacity, clip_query, cues, fade_seconds, font, overlay_track, position, stroke_color, stroke_width, style, text_color, text_size, time_base, uppercase so far); cli partial (captions come from indexed transcripts or an SRT/VTT file; the desktop also transcribes on device; only Zenvi desktop takes background_color, background_opacity, clip_query, cues, fade_seconds, font, overlay_track, position, stroke_color, stroke_width, style, text_color, text_size, time_base, uppercase so far); cloud partial (captions come from indexed transcripts or an SRT/VTT file; the desktop also transcribes on device; only Zenvi desktop takes background_color, background_opacity, clip_query, cues, fade_seconds, font, overlay_track, position, stroke_color, stroke_width, style, text_color, text_size, time_base, uppercase so far; only when ffprobe is available and the engine's assets (title templates, emoji) are bundled); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `background_color` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Colour of the box behind the text (alpha in '#RRGGBBAA' sets its opacity). Empty = the style's. (default "") |
| `background_opacity` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Opacity of the box behind the text, 0 (no box) to 1. -1 = the style's. (default -1, min -1, max 1) |
| `clipId` | string |  | Timeline clip to caption (the speaker's clip). Same as timeline_clip_id. (default "") |
| `clip_query` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Describe the clip to caption instead of an id, e.g. 'talking head'. (default "") |
| `cues` | object[] |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Captions to show, each {start, end, text} in timeline seconds (or the clip's source seconds with time_base='source'). Use for text you already have. |
| `engine` | string |  | Accepted for compatibility; not used (the transcript comes from the media index). (default "auto") |
| `fade_seconds` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Fade each caption in and out over this many seconds (0-3). -1 = the style's. (default -1, min -1, max 3) |
| `font` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Font family, e.g. 'Arial Black', 'Helvetica Neue'. Empty = the style's font. (default "") |
| `language` | string |  | Accepted for compatibility with the on-device speech tools; the transcript comes from Zenvi's media index, which already knows the language. (default "auto") |
| `maxChars` | integer |  | Longest caption, in characters, when phrasing a transcript. (default 42, min 8, max 120) |
| `maxWords` | integer |  | Longest caption, in words, when phrasing a transcript (subtitle files and cues are kept as written). (default 8, min 1, max 24) |
| `modelId` | string |  | Accepted for compatibility; not used (the transcript comes from the media index). (default "") |
| `overlay_track` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Track for the transparent 'Captions' overlay clip used when no clip is captioned. Empty = the lowest free track above the video. (default "") |
| `position` | "" \| "bottom" \| "center" \| "top" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Where the captions sit: bottom (above the safe margin, higher on vertical video), center or top. Empty = the style's (bottom). (default "") |
| `replace_existing` | boolean |  | Replace the captions a clip already has (true) or add a second caption track to it (false). (default true) |
| `srtPath` | string |  | Path of an .srt or .vtt subtitle file to burn in. With a clip its times are that clip's media time; without one, timeline time. (default "") |
| `stroke_color` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Outline colour. Empty = the style's. (default "") |
| `stroke_width` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Outline thickness relative to the text height: 0 = none, 0.03 thin, 0.09 heavy (heavy outlines only read with heavy fonts such as Arial Black). -1 = the style's. (default -1, min -1, max 0.5) |
| `style` | "boxed" \| "classic" \| "minimal" \| "reels" \| "yellow" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Look preset: classic = white text on a dark box at the bottom (subtitles); reels = big bold white text with a black outline (Instagram/TikTok/Shorts); minimal = small white text with a thin outline; yellow = yellow text with a black outline (TV subtitles); boxed = white on a solid black box. The arguments below override parts of it. (default "classic") |
| `text_color` | string |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Text colour '#RRGGBB' / '#RRGGBBAA' / 'rgba(...)' / name. Empty = the style's. (default "") |
| `text_size` | number |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Text height as a fraction of the frame's shorter side: 0.04 small, 0.05 normal subtitles, 0.075 big reel captions. 0 = the style's size. (default 0, min 0, max 0.3) |
| `time_base` | "auto" \| "timeline" \| "source" |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** What cue times mean: timeline seconds, or the clip's source (media) seconds. auto = source for subtitle files and transcripts, timeline for cues. (default "auto") |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip to caption. (default "") |
| `trackIndex` | integer |  | Caption every clip on this UI track (1 = bottom) from its transcript. 0 = not used. (default 0, min 0) |
| `uppercase` | boolean |  | **Zenvi desktop only so far.** Show the captions in capital letters. (default false) |

### add_clips_to_timeline_tool

**Add clips to timeline**. Place several project files back to back on one track in one step: the backbone of "make a 60-second vlog from these clips", "put all the beach shots on the timeline with crossfades", "make a slideshow of these photos, 3 seconds each".

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_overlap` | boolean |  | Let the result overlap other clips on the track (the receipt lists what it covers). Off by default: the tool refuses and says what is in the way. (default false) |
| `fade` | "none" \| "in" \| "out" \| "in_out" |  | Opacity fades on every clip, used instead of a transition; clips overlap by fade_seconds so the fades cross. (default "none") |
| `fade_seconds` | number |  | Fade length in seconds. (default 2, min 0.04) |
| `file_ids` | string[] |  | Project file ids to place, in timeline order (list_files_tool). Use this OR items. (default []) |
| `fit_total_seconds` | number |  | Make the whole sequence last exactly this long (e.g. 60 for a 60-second vlog) by trimming the longest clips evenly, keeping the middle of each (heads and tails are usually shaky); 0 = full lengths. (default 0, min 0) |
| `image_seconds` | number |  | How long each still image stays on screen; 0 = the Default Image Length preference. (default 0, min 0) |
| `items` | object[] |  | Files with their own in/out points, in timeline order. Use this OR file_ids. (default []) |
| `min_clip_seconds` | number |  | Shortest a clip may be trimmed to by fit_total_seconds. (default 1, min 0.1) |
| `order` | "as_given" \| "shuffle" \| "name" |  | Order on the timeline: as given, shuffled, or by file name. (default "as_given") |
| `start_seconds` | number |  | Timeline time of the first clip; -1 = right after the last clip already on the track (0 on an empty track). (default -1) |
| `track` | string |  | Track to fill: UI track number (1 = bottom), name, or layer number. Empty = the selected track, else the bottom track. (default "") |
| `transition` | string |  | Transition between consecutive clips: '' = hard cuts, 'fade' = crossfade, 'random', or a transition name such as 'wipe_left_to_right' or 'circle_in_to_out' (list_transitions_tool). (default "") |
| `transition_seconds` | number |  | Length of each transition; clips overlap by this much. 0 = the Default Transition Length preference. (default 0, min 0) |
| `zoom` | "none" \| "in" \| "out" \| "random" |  | Slow zoom on every clip (Ken Burns): in = 100% to 125%, out = 125% to 100%, random = random zoom and pan. (default "none") |

| `shift_seconds` | number |  | Move every cue later (positive) or earlier (negative) to fix sync. (default 0, min -3600, max 3600) |

| `text_size` | number |  | Text height as a fraction of the frame's shorter side: 0.04 small, 0.05 normal subtitles, 0.075 big reel captions. 0 = the style's size. (default 0, min 0, max 0.3) |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | The captioned clip (when it has one caption track). (default "") |
| `uppercase` | boolean |  | Turn every cue's text into capital letters. (default false) |

### build_reel_tool

**Build a reel** (direct tool). Cut a finished short-form video (Reels, TikTok, Shorts, ads) in one step from media already in the project: shots cut on the music's beats, camera moves, flashes, a look, an opening hook title, shot labels, an end card and the music faded out.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | "hype" \| "cinematic" \| "highlight" \| "match_cut" \| "minimal" \| "editorial" \| "retro" \| "ui_promo" \| "editorial_motion" \| "product_callout" \| "tutorial" |  | How the reel is cut and looks (default hype). hype: Energetic montage for launches, sports, events and travel: fast cuts on the beat, flashes on the downbeats, punchy colour. cinematic: Moody, filmic montage for stories, brands and places: steady 2-beat shots, slow push-ins, grain, fades. highlight: The best moments of the person's own clips (games, trips, events): cut on the beat, building to the big moment. match_cut: Shots that share a shape or pose cut on every beat (circles, hands, horizons): the frame stays still so the shapes line up. minimal: Slow, airy edit for wellness, food, interiors and products: long holds, gentle moves, soft fades. editorial: Graphic, magazine-like cut for fashion, design and tech: crisp cuts on 1/2 beats, labels on the shots, clean contrast. retro: Nostalgic camcorder feel for vlogs, throwbacks and music: tape artefacts, warm colour, super 8 grain. ui_promo: Motion-designed product promo for apps and tools: a search bar types the hook, footage rises in rounded UI cards and a pointer clicks, a word list scrolls in a selection box, a logo end card. Give `words` for the word list. editorial_motion: Graphic specimen-sheet motion for fashion, design, food and objects: the hook as big kinetic type on a gridded sheet (a letter swapped for an image tile), labelled crop boxes over a shot that lift into a row, kinetic words, a closing card. Red, black and paper with one blue. product_callout: Technical product reveal: each product shot on a dark field with a soft glow, an 'ANATOMY: NAME' heading, leader lines drawing out to feature labels, one per beat, then a closing card. Give `words` as features ('Foam core: 212 g'). tutorial: A how-to in steps (9:16 first): the hook on grid paper, then one step per clip (the footage in a bordered card, a numbered caption from `labels`, a label box with an arrow from `words`), ending on 'Save this'. |
| `file_ids` | string[] |  | Media-bin videos and images to use, in story order; the last one closes the reel. Default: every video and image in the bin, in bin order. |
| `music_file_id` | string |  | Music in the media bin to cut to. Default: the longest audio file in the bin. Without music the cuts follow the style's own tempo. |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | Target length, seconds (default per style, 12-20). The reel ends on the last downbeat before it. (min 4, max 120) |
| `hook` | string |  | Opening title over the first shots: 2-6 punchy words. |
| `end_card` | string |  | Closing title over the last shot (a call to action, a name, a date). |
| `end_card_subtitle` | string |  | A smaller line under the end card. |
| `labels` | string[] |  | Small labels shown on each file's shots, in file_ids order ("" for none). Motion styles: the card captions (ui_promo), crop labels (editorial_motion), step captions (tutorial). |
| `words` | string[] |  | Motion styles only: the scrolling word list (ui_promo), kinetic words (editorial_motion), the features as 'Name: value' (product_callout), each step's label box (tutorial). |
| `beats` | number[] |  | Beat times of the music in seconds (e.g. from detect_beats_tool) instead of analysing it here. |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Clear the timeline first when it already has clips (they are removed in the same undo step). |

### add_motion_template_tool

**Add a motion template** (direct tool). Place one motion-design template on the timeline, timed to the beat: UI cards that slide in with depth, a search field that types, a scrolling word list with a selection box, labelled crop boxes over a shot, a product callout with leader lines, kinetic type with image tiles, a tutorial step card, a grid background or an end card.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | "ui_cards" \| "type_search" \| "word_scroll" \| "crop_labels" \| "callout" \| "kinetic_type" \| "step_card" \| "grid_background" \| "end_card" | yes | Which template. ui_cards: Up to three rounded UI cards (footage or photos inside, or text cards) rise into a fan (landscape) or slide into a cascade (portrait), one per beat, with depth; with a button, a pointer glides to the front card and clicks it (press, ripple, check), then the camera pushes in. Reads file_ids (card media, in order), labels (a caption per card; a card without a file is a text card titled by its label), subtitle (text cards' second line), button (what the pointer clicks). type_search: A search field rises in, the phrase types letter by letter with a blinking caret and lands on a beat; suggestions drop open under it a row per half beat; then the button presses (or the first suggestion is selected) and a focus ring lights up. Reads text (the phrase, one line), button (the button label), subtitle (a prompt above the field), tag (a brand row on top: its mark and name), labels (up to 4 suggestions that drop open under the field; the press selects the first), backdrop. word_scroll: A column of big words scrolls up one word per beat; each scroll lands on the beat with the word held in a selection box (handles and a size readout), the other words dimmed; an optional lead line reads into the word. Reads words (2-10, in order), text (a lead line: beside the word in landscape, above it in portrait), backdrop. crop_labels: A shot fills the frame and pushes in; labelled crop boxes snap onto it one per beat; then a paper scrim covers it and the crops lift out of the shot into a row of labelled tiles. Reads file_ids (the shot: the first file), boxes (frame boxes, 0-1; default a spread), labels (one per box; default DETAIL 01…), tag (the default labels' prefix), variant (boxes: no row). callout: A product shot on a dark field with a soft halo and a glowing 'ANATOMY: NAME' heading over a rule that draws on; then one callout per beat: a dot pops on the product, a leader line draws out and a label (index, name, value) slides in. Reads file_ids (the product: the first file), text (the product name), tag (the heading's prefix, default ANATOMY), labels (callout names, 1-4), values (their second lines), points (anchors on the product picture, 0-1). kinetic_type: A big grotesk headline lands one word per beat, each word popping in; * in the text becomes an image tile (a word or a letter replaced by footage or a photo); optional highlighter swipe behind a word and a small tag after the last word. Reads text (the headline; * = image tile), file_ids (tile media, used in turn), highlight (word index), tag, align (left \| center), position (top \| center \| bottom). step_card: A tutorial step: the footage rises into a rounded card with an ink border and a hard shadow, a numbered caption pops in under it, then a small label box appears and an arrow draws from it to a point in the footage. Reads file_ids (the step's footage: the first file), text (the caption), step (its number, default 1), tag (the label box's text), points (where the arrow points in the footage, 0-1; default the upper right), subtitle (a still header at the top, e.g. the video's hook). grid_background: A still, full-frame field: grid paper (paper), an editorial sheet with column grid, ruler ticks, registration marks and corner labels (editorial), a dark dot grid (dots) or a flat colour (plain). Reads variant (paper \| editorial \| dots \| plain, default from the palette), labels (editorial: up to 4 corner labels). end_card: The closing card. logo: a brand mark pops in, the name slides out beside it, the subtitle rises; save: a bookmark drops in and 'Save this' lands with a highlighter swipe; plain: a tag, the title and the subtitle rise in turn. Draws its own backdrop. Reads text (title or brand name; save defaults to 'Save this'), subtitle, tag (plain), variant (logo \| save \| plain), align (plain), backdrop. |
| `position_seconds` | number |  | Timeline start, seconds (default 0). Entrances land on the beats after it. (min 0) |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | Length, seconds (default: the template's natural length in beats). (min 0.5, max 120) |
| `palette` | "ui_light" \| "ui_dark" \| "editorial" \| "callout" \| "tutorial" |  | Colours: ui_light, ui_dark, editorial (paper, ink, red, one blue), callout (dark, hot accent), tutorial (grid paper, ink, highlighter). Default per template. |

| `values` | string[] |  | callout: the second line of each callout (a spec, a number). |
| `points` | object[] |  | callout: anchor points on the product picture (0-1 from its top left); step_card: the point the label's arrow points at. |
| `boxes` | object[] |  | crop_labels: boxes on the frame (centre x, y and size w, h, 0-1). Default: a spread of boxes. |
| `button` | string |  | A button's label: type_search's search button, ui_cards' button the pointer clicks. |
| `tag` | string |  | A small tag: kinetic_type's (e.g. NO. 01), end_card plain's, step_card's label box, type_search's brand row, crop_labels' label prefix, callout's heading prefix (default ANATOMY). |
| `step` | integer |  | step_card: the step number. (min 1, max 99) |
| `highlight` | integer |  | kinetic_type: index of the word the highlighter marks. (min 0, max 30) |

## Divergences from the desktop

Deliberate differences from the zenvi-core handlers:

- **add_title_tool**: The text also replaces every line whose placeholder matches the first line's. Reflection templates (Bar_1, the default) draw a mirrored copy first; the desktop's `_set_svg_text` (agent_tools/titles.py:32) fills only that copy and blanks the real line, so its titles render upside down.
- **add_clip_to_timeline_tool**: Appending (no position_seconds) butts the clip against the last clip on the track. The desktop places it at `last_end + _one_frame` (tool_handlers.py:2726), leaving a one-frame black/silent gap.
- **add_clip_to_timeline_tool and the tools that place through it**: A host that cannot watch frames (no frame rendering or no Zenvi backend) counts as "not watched": a duration-only trim of a full video is refused instead of placing the first N seconds, and the result never says "(watched)". The desktop's watch falls back softly and places the window.
- **watch (add_clip_to_timeline_tool, slice_clip_at_best_match_tool, search_clip_scenes_tool, watch_clip_window_tool)**: Up to 12 frames rendered by the host; no ffmpeg scene-cut detection (shot cuts are always reported as none) and no near-duplicate frame dedupe (watch_window.py extract_watch_window).
- **apply_transition_tool**: clip2 defaults to the next clip on clip1's track instead of `Error: clip2_id is required` (tool_handlers.py:6645); no transition_name means fade (the desktop took the first file in its transitions folder).
- **reindex_project_file_tool**: "Already indexed" reads the current `ai_metadata.index` block (legacy `twelvelabs` as fallback); the desktop reads only `twelvelabs` (tool_handlers.py:7344). Re-uploading for indexing is not available on the web.
- **add_marker_tool / list_markers_tool**: A marker's name is stored as `label`, the key the web editor shows; zenvi-core develop stores `name` (track_ops.add_marker). list_markers_tool reads either.
- **add_title_tool / add_captions_tool**: Templates are the bundled catalog, read by basename only (the desktop joined a bare template name into its titles folder unchecked, agent_tools/titles.py:81); an absolute .svg path is read through the host's storage.
- **add_animated_title_tool / list_title_templates_tool kind=animated**: The Blender templates are drawn as 2D titles: an SVG title animated with clip keyframes (scale, position, rotation, opacity) and the engine's Glow, Blur and LensFlare effects, so they render the same in the browser, the CLI and the cloud and stay editable. Extrusion, bevel, lighting, particles and 3D camera moves are approximated or dropped. Template names, parameters, defaults, validation and the length (template frames × length_multiplier, remapped for the project frame rate like Blender) are the desktop's; earth, magic_wand, snow and picture_frames_4 are 3D scenes and are refused as desktop-only; spacemovie_intro and colors place three clips in a row; timeout_seconds is accepted and unused. kind=animated lists `renders_here` and `look` per template and a `renderer` block where the desktop reports its Blender setup.
- **edit_title_tool**: The edited title is a new Project Files entry that takes the old one's place in every clip and in the bin (scope=all_clips), in the same undo step; the desktop points the same entry at the new SVG and keeps its file_id. Web hosts store media by content and never change the bytes behind a file id. The receipt's file_id is the new entry's.
- **titles, captions and timers: fonts**: Fonts are taken as given: the hosts cannot list installed fonts (the browser and resvg each fall back on their own). The desktop checks names against Qt's font database, suggests close matches for an unknown font, replaces a template font that is not installed with the Title Editor's fallback, and drops a caption preset's font (thinning its outline) when that font is missing.
- **list_title_templates_tool**: kind=static lists the 50 bundled templates; the web has no user template folder. kind=project reads each title through the host's storage (bundled emoji through the assets).
- **add_emoji_tool / search_emojis_tool**: The desktop's 1,239 OpenMoji SVGs ship with the engine (assets/emojis, minified without changing what they draw; scripts/gen-emojis.mjs) and are stored as `@emojis/<file>` like the desktop stores them. There is no user emoji folder (group 'user' finds nothing). duration_seconds 0 is 10 s, the desktop's Default Image Length preference default.
- **list_captions_tool / edit_captions_tool / remove_captions_tool**: They work on Caption effects, as on desktop develop (captions made by Zenvi desktop or with the Caption effect); the engine's add_captions_tool still places one title per cue (the earlier desktop behaviour), which these tools do not list. With no target the project's only caption track is used: the web has no effect selection to pick from.
- **get_transcript_tool, export_captions_tool, add_captions_tool**: Transcripts come from the indexed `ai_metadata.transcript_cues`; word timings inside a cue are estimated by character count (`transcriptionSource: "index_cues"`, `wordTiming: "estimated"`). The desktop runs on-device ASR.
- **remove_silence_tool**: Speech windows come from the desktop's energy VAD run on the host's RMS envelope (AudioHost.analyzeAudio), not from on-device VAD models.
- **web-only arguments**: Hosts without a playhead or local file paths, and the CLI, need a few arguments the desktop's schemas do not have (scripts/tool-schema-overlay.json `web_extra_props`): add_marker_tool label/text and add_track_tool label (older names for `name`), save_project_tool path, set_clip_volume_tool volume/gain/db, set_clip_speed_tool clip_id/factor/direction (the web's older speed tool: one clip id, speed, backward = reverse), watch_clip_tool file_id/timeline_clip_id, import_stock_media_tool position_seconds/track/duration_seconds/start_seconds (place the import). Every argument the desktop accepts is accepted; the ones only the desktop handles so far are refused (see Not ported yet).
- **desktop defaults the web does not follow yet**: save_project_tool and export_video_tool replace an existing file (the CLI's) where the desktop refuses unless overwrite=true; add_title_tool never shrinks long lines (desktop fit_text=true); add_captions_tool adds a new caption group where the desktop replaces the clip's captions (replace_existing=true); new_project_tool / open_project_tool have no unsaved-changes guard (every web surface autosaves, so discard_unsaved is accepted as is); generate_tts_and_add_to_timeline_tool defaults to the track below the picture, where the desktop picks or creates a free narration track.
- **tools zenvi-core develop rewrote as editor tools**: get_project_info_tool, list_markers_tool, get_export_settings_tool, set_export_setting_tool, new/open/save_project_tool, play_tool, add_track_tool, add_marker_tool, export_video_tool, generate_tts_and_add_to_timeline_tool, add_effect_tool, add_title_tool, set_keyframes_tool, set_project_setting_tool and add_captions_tool take develop's schemas; their results keep the earlier text and receipts (develop answers with structured receipts), set_export_setting_tool stores any key (develop checks keys and aliases), and set_keyframes_tool animates the seven earlier properties (develop: any keyframable clip property).
- **split_file_add_clip_tool**: require_visual_match reads true/false; the desktop's `bool(...)` treats the string "false" as true (tool_handlers.py:2370).
- **wait_for_editor_job_tool (desktop MCP extra, #237)**: Pending, and likely to stay so: tool calls here run to completion inside the call, so there is never a detached editor job; the name gets the standard not-available refusal.
- **argument coercion**: As zenvi-core normalize_args, plus numbers/booleans become strings for string-only properties (MCP clients send typed JSON). Tools that are editor tools on the desktop coerce like its @editor_tool registry (`_registry.coerce_args`): case-insensitive enums, "1.5s", comma-separated or JSON lists, "y"/"n"; an empty string or null for an argument that cannot hold it means its default where the desktop refuses it, and a value that cannot be coerced is refused in the web's words (`Invalid arguments for …`) rather than the registry's.
- **add_clips_to_timeline_tool**: image_seconds=0 and transition_seconds=0 mean the desktop's default Default Image Length (10 s) and Default Transition Length (1 s): the web has no preferences.
- **separate_clip_audio_tool**: With to_track the audio clip goes straight there. The desktop first splits it onto the track below (creating a track when the clip is on the bottom one) and then moves it, which can leave that new track empty.
- **set_clip_audio_video_tool**: The web timeline draws the waveform of every clip with sound and has no per-clip switch: waveform=show changes nothing and waveform=hide is refused (in words the Assistant retries without it). The desktop stores waveform samples in the clip (`ui.audio_data`).
- **reverse_clip_tool**: A clip on a locked track is refused; the desktop's handler reverses it anyway (its Time menu skips the lock check).
- **summary previews**: `…` is written as U+2026; the desktop's file had the mojibake `ΓÇª` (ai_metadata_utils.build_summary_preview).
